article_title: Effect of digital virtual reality simulator on pre-clinical dental surgical skill training: a retrospective study.
citation: Ren Jian-gang, Li Rui-fang, Zhang Wei, Yu Zi-li, Chen Gang. (2025). Effect of digital virtual reality simulator on pre-clinical dental surgical skill training: a retrospective study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07747-x
title: Digital Virtual Reality Simulator (DVRS) for Dental Surgical Skills Training
description: The DVRS is China's first multifunctional VR platform for dental surgical skill training, comprising the Oral Virtual PC-based Teaching Platform (Unidraw Stomatology Digital Virtual Training System) and the Oral Surgery Simulator (Unidraw Virtual Classic Edition). It builds "a complete 3D patient oral model", lets students practice the full diagnosis-and-treatment process online or with a simulator using "dual-hand force feedback technology", and its evaluation system "provides real-time scoring and generates feedback of each student's operation, supporting replay for review". In the study it replaced manikin-based preclinical training for the 2018 cohort.
requirements: Instructors received dedicated training in the technology before preclinical sessions
Specialized equipment and smooth computer operation
constraints: The authors note limitations including "the requirement of specialized equipment, smooth computer operation, and a higher investment cost"
target_learners: fourth-year undergraduate stomatology students in preclinical surgical training
target_learning_goals: dental surgical skills such as local anesthesia, tooth extraction, abscess incision drainage, and suturing
clinical diagnosis-and-treatment workflow and patient communication
examples: The 2018 cohort used the DVRS across a 48-hour course covering local anesthesia, tooth extraction, abscess incision drainage, and suturing, with real-time scoring during operations
key_sources: Ren Jian-gang, Li Rui-fang, Zhang Wei, Yu Zi-li, Chen Gang. (2025). Effect of digital virtual reality simulator on pre-clinical dental surgical skill training: a retrospective study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07747-x

article_title: Experiences and perceptions of students in occupational therapy regarding the use of desktop virtual environments-based simulation: a qualitative study.
citation: Wang Zhizhuo, Wu Peiyun, Shi Shaoyun, Zhang Weiwei, Lin Cheng. (2025). Experiences and perceptions of students in occupational therapy regarding the use of desktop virtual environments-based simulation: a qualitative study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07495-y
title: D-VSim: a desktop virtual environments-based simulation platform for occupational therapy ADL training
description: D-VSim is a desktop VE-based simulation learning platform developed by Fujian Medical University for the occupational therapy experiential laboratory course, accessed via a browser link with a user ID and password. The article states "The D-VSim was developed by Fujian Medical University and was applied in the occupational therapy experiential laboratory course to healthcare professional students studying occupational therapy". Its ADL training packet contains 10 modules, including Grooming, Dressing, Feeding, Toilet use, Bathing, and Bed mobility, with scenarios simulated to match the Chinese clinical context, online quizzes after module tasks, and a performance report after all modules.
requirements: Students unfamiliar with the platform received approximately 10 min of teacher-guided orientation prior to immersion in the ADL training packet.
target_learning_goals: Activity of Daily Living (ADL) training skills
applying theoretical knowledge to simulated clinical practice
examples: Students used indications displayed in the left column to instruct a simulated patient with right hemiplegia through bed mobility from supine to left-side lying in the Bed mobility module.
key_sources: Wang Zhizhuo, Wu Peiyun, Shi Shaoyun, Zhang Weiwei, Lin Cheng. (2025). Experiences and perceptions of students in occupational therapy regarding the use of desktop virtual environments-based simulation: a qualitative study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07495-y

article_title: Multi-perspective analysis of daVinci surgical virtual reality training: a prospective randomized controlled study.
citation: Wang Rong, Zheng Nan, Liang Yujing, Cui Haoxin, Ren Tong, Xing Wenhui, Li Yanghui. (2025). Multi-perspective analysis of daVinci surgical virtual reality training: a prospective randomized controlled study. Journal of Robotic Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11701-025-02309-1
title: Define simulator training proficiency as repeated expert-benchmarked task performance before testing skill outcomes
description: The article operationalizes VR training to proficiency on the daVinci simulator: trainees repeat each selected task until reaching an expert-derived benchmark. Proficiency was defined as "each trainee operating each task 10 or more times and scoring 85 or more consecutively three times during training". This criterion-based definition anchors the trial's comparison of trained versus untrained participants.
requirements: Training tasks selected with expert input and an expert-benchmarked proficiency score (two robotic surgery specialists set the standard)
A simulator scoring system that rates each task attempt objectively
constraints: The proficiency definition was applied to six basic-skill tasks on one simulator platform; the study notes dVSS scores may not fully reflect real surgical skill acquisition
target_learners: surgical residents and fellows learning robotic surgery
examples: The VR-training group trained on the dVSS simulator (XI) across six tasks until meeting the proficiency criterion, then all subjects completed six experimental tasks on the simulator (SI) three times while wearing EEG equipment
key_sources: Wang Rong, Zheng Nan, Liang Yujing, Cui Haoxin, Ren Tong, Xing Wenhui, Li Yanghui. (2025). Multi-perspective analysis of daVinci surgical virtual reality training: a prospective randomized controlled study. Journal of Robotic Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11701-025-02309-1

article_title: The Society of European Robotic Gynaecological Surgery (SERGS) Pilot Curriculum for robot assisted gynecological surgery.
citation: Rusch Peter, Kimmig Rainer, Lecuru Fabrice, Persson Jan, Ponce Jordi, Degueldre Michel, Verheijen René. (2017). The Society of European Robotic Gynaecological Surgery (SERGS) Pilot Curriculum for robot assisted gynecological surgery. Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00404-017-4612-5
title: DVSS virtual reality training console with Mimic software and MScore metrics
description: The DaVinci training console (DVSS) equipped with Mimic training software was used for virtual exercises during the intensive training week. The article states the software "uses comprehensive metrics and experienced surgeon data in the MScore" and that it "has been tested for face, construct and predicative validity," meaning it resembles the real-life situation, discriminates the ability tested for, and estimates future candidate performance. Virtual training was encouraged but not mandatory in part 1 due to availability at host institutes.
requirements: Access to a DaVinci training console with Mimic software at the training institution
constraints: Virtual procedural training was performed rarely due to limited simulator access at home centers or because it was found too time-consuming in daily routine
target_learners: Gynecology fellows training in robotic surgery
target_learning_goals: Robotic console technical skills such as endo-wrist manipulation, energy dissection, and needle driving
examples: Fellows completed standardized exercises such as Matchboard 2, Energy Switch 2, and Tubes, with overall scores recorded at baseline and after 5 days
key_sources: Rusch Peter, Kimmig Rainer, Lecuru Fabrice, Persson Jan, Ponce Jordi, Degueldre Michel, Verheijen René. (2017). The Society of European Robotic Gynaecological Surgery (SERGS) Pilot Curriculum for robot assisted gynecological surgery. Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00404-017-4612-5
